title: 30+ common Spanish phrases for your trip to Mexico
summary: Using Spanish on your trip to Mexico is a great way to connect with locals. Here are basic Spanish phrases especially for travelers!
body_markdown:
The language you’ll hear most often in Mexico is Spanish, or español


. There are also many indigenous languages—including[Nahuatl](https://blog.duolingo.com/language-families-overview/#uto-aztecan) and[Mayan languages](https://blog.duolingo.com/language-families-overview/#mayan) —spoken throughout the country!


## Spanish 101


**You don’t have to be fluent to have fun with Spanish.**
You’re on vacation, so don’t stress! Enjoy using the Spanish you know and see what else you learn along the way.


**It’s the effort that counts.**
Using some Spanish shows locals that you’re interested in their culture and community.


**Study smart, not hard.**
Focus on the most useful Spanish words and phrases, and worry less about getting every grammar detail right. A few key words go a long way!


hello hola


excuse me disculpe


(formal)
disculpa


(informal)

My name is ___. Me llamo ___.


## Asking for help


Do you speak English? ¿Usted habla inglés?


(formal)
¿Hablas inglés?


(informal)


Where is the bathroom? ¿Dónde está el baño?


I’m sorry, I don’t understand. Lo siento, no entiendo.


Can you help me? ¿Me puede ayudar?


(formal)
¿Me puedes ayudar?


(informal)


I’m lost. Estoy perdido.


(for a man)
Estoy perdida.


(for a woman)

Where are the pyramids?

¿Dónde está el museo?

## Local language


***Buenos días* or *buenas tardes***
It’s considered polite to greet people with buenos días


(good morning) or buenas tardes


(good afternoon/good evening) when you enter stores, cafés, or souvenir shops.


***Chido* and *padre***
Before you leave Mexico, you too will be using chido


and padre


to say *cool* !


***Zócalo***
A zócalo


is a main square or central plaza, and it’s an especially important landmark in Mexico City.


***¿Pica mucho?***
If you’re not used to spicy cuisine, you might find some Mexican food too fiery for you! Remember to ask ¿Pica mucho?


if you want to know if a dish is spicy.
